body:
Can confirm I'm also running into this issue, with both ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver. Having either causes error spam, although they both otherwise work as intended.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d89a50cf-c95c-4378-832b-31c9ed3a4116)

153 errors in console caused by 3 format loaders + 3 format savers.

This also happens on 4.5 dev. Additionally I seem to get the following error as well (On 4.4 and 4.5 dev)

`ERROR: editor/editor_node.cpp:1486 - Condition "res.is_null()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN`.

It seems custom resource format loaders are being unloaded. Reloading the project will always fix the issue, typically until next build. Sometimes everything works after the `does not inherit 'ResourceFormatLoader'` error presents. But if a ERR_CANT_OPEN is thrown too a project reload is required

I've found a fix which removes the errors, but causes you to need to disable then re-enable the editor plugin after each project re-build. This can be worked around by using a static class with a static constructor to register your classes. I may know the reason why this issue is happening although it will require confirmation.

Firstly the fix:

Open up your project, go to all your ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver classes and remove the [GlobalClass] annotation. I'm not sure if it's needed, but I also add the [Tool] annotation to each of these classes.

Then, navigate to your project's ".godot" folder and delete "global_script_class_cache.cfg".

Rebuild your project. If all goes well there shouldn't be any errors.

I think the reason these errors are happening has to do with this:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85f88114-e3b6-4815-9ab0-b5f185dd6a76)

If what this documentation is saying is true, ResourceFormatLoaders (and presumably savers) are automatically registered if they are created in GDScript. For this to be the case, the format loaders/savers would have to be recognised from and then loaded from the global class cache, which coincides with the fact that removing the C# classes from the global class cache stopped the errors. I think that how ever this feature is implemented, it's incorrectly identifying C# format loaders/savers as GDScript ones, and then attempting and failing to register them. This is also probably why the error mentions the path to the script file, because it is most likely trying to load the script file, which wouldn't make sense when registering the loader/saver in code.

Edit: It seems [GlobalClass] is needed to allow the loaders/savers to be re-registered after rebuild, so I guess _EnterTree doesn't actually get called on project rebuild? So the application is persisting the fact that it has format loaders/savers registered through project rebuilds, and is trying to reload them through the global class cache?
It seems that ResourceFormatLoaders are automatically registered if they are global classes even in C#, which means that theres no need to register them in code. The issue persists regardless.
